messages:
maria.devex: Hey — quick pattern question. We're scripting nightly jobs that need to 1) pick a profile from a shared store, 2) open a long-lived streaming session (>30m) to the hosted API, and 3) transparently refresh creds without dropping the stream. Any recommended CLI/profile patterns?

alex.eng: short answer: avoid rewriting the on-disk profile while the stream is active. prefer env override or a file-per-run pattern.

sam.ops: +1. In CI we create an ephemeral file and point RW_CONFIG to it. that way you can rotate token in place for new runs without touching other processes.

jen.sdk: fwiw the CLI honors RW_PROFILE env var and RW_CONFIG (path) as overrides. example:

```
export RW_CONFIG=/tmp/rw-job-$CI_JOB_ID.yaml
export RW_PROFILE=team-staging
redwood chat --model gpt-4-streaming --stream
```

If you need to refresh token mid-stream, the current runtime won't auto-reload the config file for an existing connection. you need an out-of-band credential refresh mechanism (see below).

maria.devex: ok that aligns with what I feared. what's the out-of-band approach? can we swap credentials in KMS/kube secret and have the client pick it up?

sam.ops: you can implement a local token proxy. pattern is: long-lived process opens a socket to local agent which holds the active token and proxies requests to redwood endpoint. when secret rotates, agent updates header for new connections. Existing streaming connections keep old token (can't change mid-TCP), so you need to spin a short-lived reconnect strategy that is transparent to higher-level code.

alex.eng: another option: short streaming window + automatic reconnect with resume tokens. Our SDK supports reconnect with an ephemeral resume cursor for chat (ask @jen for details). basically: if connection drops, client asks server to resume from last token id. meaning you can rotate credentials between reconnects.

jen.sdk: tiny example of reconnect loop (psuedo):

```
while true; do
  redwood chat --stream --cursor $LAST_CURSOR || true
  sleep 1
  # update LAST_CURSOR from last event
done
```

Note: keep retry backoff so you don't hammer during rotation.

maria.devex: good — want to make sure we don't accidentally leak other teams' profiles. any secure-file best practices?

sam.ops: store ephemeral configs in a per-job dir with 0700 perms and remove immediately after. in k8s use projected serviceaccount tokens or CSI to mount per-pod secrets. do not write tokens to shared $HOME/.redwood/* at runtime.

alex.eng: small PS/CMD note for Windows agents: RW_CONFIG env works in PowerShell: `setx RW_CONFIG C:\tmp\rw.yaml` but for ephemeral CI runs prefer `powershell -c "$env:RW_CONFIG='C:\\temp\\rw-$env:BUILD_ID.yaml'; redwood chat ..."` (avoid global setx).

maria.devex: thanks. last question: profile inheritance — can we have a base profile with common fields and overlay per-job?

jen.sdk: cli doesn't have layered profiles natively. you can implement simple overlays by templating YAML:

```
# base.yaml
api_host: api.redwood.local
retries: 3

# overlay.yaml
profile: team-x
token: <from-vault>
```

Then render into /tmp/rw-merged.yaml with `yq` or `python` before running. keep it ephemeral.

sam.ops: also consider using the CLI's `redwood auth login --token-file /path` helper so you don't inject tokens inline into the YAML (reduces accidental logs). the helper writes to the config path you control.

maria.devex: perfect. i'll draft a template + example scripts for the infra repo and link back here. will ping for review. :raised_hands:

ci-bot: Created PR #432: devex/ci/ephemeral-rw-config — ready for review :gear:
